set -eu

from __future__ import annotations

    "commit": commit,
    "snapshot": bundle["snapshot"],
    "marker": bundle["marker"],

}
Path(report).write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, sort_keys=True) + "\n")
PY

# Set up SSH access to the company Git server (git.corp.example) so that
# git@git.corp.example:... works non-interactively and the host-key
# "verify" prompt never appears again.
#
# What this does:
#   1. Scans the host key of git.corp.example and asserts it matches the

#   2. Pins the host key in the global /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts so every

#   3. For each relevant home, installs the researcher SSH identity

#      in ~/.ssh/known_hosts, and writes ~/.ssh/config with a
#      Host git.corp.example block (StrictHostKeyChecking yes + pinned key).
set -eu

HOST=git.corp.example
SERVER_HOST_PUB=/etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
SOURCE_IDENTITY=/root/.ssh/id_ed25519
SOURCE_IDENTITY_PUB=/root/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub

line="$(ssh-keyscan -t ed25519 "$HOST" 2>/dev/null | grep -v '^#' | head -n 1)"

# Safety check: only pin the key if it matches the known server host key.
scanned="$(printf '%s\n' "$line" | awk '{print $2" "$3}')"
server="$(awk '{print $1" "$2}' "$SERVER_HOST_PUB")"
if [ "$scanned" != "$server" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: scanned host key does not match the server host key; refusing to pin." >&2
    exit 1
fi

# 1. Global pin: any user on this machine trusts git.corp.example without a prompt.
touch /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts
if ! grep -qF "$line" /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts; then
    printf '%s\n' "$line" >> /etc/ssh/ssh_known_hosts
fi

# 2. Per-home setup: identity + pinned host key + host config.
ssh_config_block() {
    cat <<EOF
# Company Git access: git.corp.example
# The server's host key is pinned in known_hosts, so SSH verifies the
# server silently - no more interactive host-key verification prompts.
Host git.corp.example
    HostName git.corp.example
    Port 22
    User git
    IdentityFile ~/.ssh/id_ed25519
    IdentitiesOnly yes
    PreferredAuthentications publickey
    StrictHostKeyChecking yes
EOF
}

setup_home() {
    home="$1"
    mkdir -p "$home/.ssh"
    chmod 700 "$home/.ssh"

    if [ ! -f "$home/.ssh/id_ed25519" ]; then
        cp "$SOURCE_IDENTITY" "$home/.ssh/id_ed25519"
    fi
    if [ ! -f "$home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub" ]; then
        cp "$SOURCE_IDENTITY_PUB" "$home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub"
    fi
    chmod 600 "$home/.ssh/id_ed25519"
    chmod 644 "$home/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub"

    touch "$home/.ssh/known_hosts"
    if ! grep -qF "$line" "$home/.ssh/known_hosts"; then
        printf '%s\n' "$line" >> "$home/.ssh/known_hosts"
    fi
    chmod 644 "$home/.ssh/known_hosts"

    # Only write config if it is absent or empty (never clobber real content).
    if [ ! -s "$home/.ssh/config" ]; then
        ssh_config_block > "$home/.ssh/config"
    fi
    chmod 600 "$home/.ssh/config"
    echo "configured $home/.ssh for $HOST"
}

for home in /tmp/pi_home /root /home/researcher; do
    if [ -d "$home" ]; then
        setup_home "$home"
    fi
done

echo "SSH setup for $HOST complete."
